meta.source_count_method: distinct URLs cited in RULES.md and GUIDE.md, trailing punctuation trimmed
meta.notes: Rules adopted from GUIDE.md are tagged unverified with page URL as source. All other rules retain their original Stage 0 tags.

recruiter_behavior.recruiter_scan_gap_before_tailoring: Most resumes fail the 7-second scan when contact, most recent role, or education is buried.

page_limits._note: The budget is ONE PAGE for every level. It rises by research_bump, capped at researched_max, only when the profile carries research (publications) -- those are evidence, not padding. `max` is the budget the app enforces (unverified product decision). `researched_max` is the figure the research supports (verified where marked); it is a ceiling for the bump, not a target.

layout_rules: no tables, text boxes, columns, icons, images, charts
consistent date format (e.g. 'Jan 2024' or '2024-01'); avoid apostrophe-year shorthand like '21; always include the month

section_order.fallback_note: RULES.md section 3 never said where an experienced candidate's achievements belong, so they were silently dropped by any renderer that iterated section_order exactly. achievements_awards is now listed for both levels, and fallback_append is the belt-and-braces rule: a populated section the order did not place is appended, never discarded. Data loss is not an acceptable rendering outcome.
section_order.achievements_placement_note: Position of Achievements for experienced candidates is our design decision, not a sourced rule. RULES.md section 3 lists the experienced order without it and does not cover the case. End of the resume is the conventional placement.

date_styles._note: The four display styles a template may pick. Stored dates are always canonical ('YYYY-MM', 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'Present' -- see models.normalise_date); only the rendering differs, so every one of these styles is accepted on input without ambiguity. 'month_year' is the default because rules.json ats.layout_rules allows either form and both templates pick it today; switching a template to another style is this file's edit, not a code change.
date_styles.present_label_note: The wording for a role that has no end date. 'Present' is used because it is the form sheetsresume.com and most Indian and US templates use, and because it is a word rather than a second date, so nobody has to guess whether the role ended. Any of Present / Current / Now / Ongoing / Till date is accepted on input and all of them store as this one label (see models.PRESENT_WORDS).

blank.label: Blank skeleton - every section, including a summary
blank.note: Mirrors section_order above, which is backed by cited sources.

sheets.label: SheetsResume - no summary, one Interests line at the end
sheets.source: https://www.reddit.com/r/jobs/comments/1c1mqp0/ - u/SheetsGiggles, self-described former Fortune 100 recruiter; https://sheetsresume.com/advice
sheets.note: The source states plainly that a summary or objective 'will be skipped, and it's space that can be used better'. Adopted as the default template per decision (2). Source remains unverified (single source).

resume_templates.why_not_merge: The two templates are kept separate on purpose. Silently dropping Summary would override a verified, cited rule with one source's opinion; the honest resolution is to let the user pick, and to record the disagreement where the renderer can see it.

tips.title: The human screener is the real gate
tips.body: An ATS is built to never block a qualified candidate, so it errs toward letting people through. The person reading is under pressure not to waste a call on an unsuitable CV, so they cut hard: no relevant title, a typo, four pages, or anything they cannot skim in seconds. Write for that reader.

tips.title: Aim for one page
tips.body: One page is the budget, for every level. It rises only when you have publications or research to list, because those are evidence rather than padding. Space spent on a summary is space not spent on evidence.

tips.title: Numbers carry the claim
tips.body: Reduced p99 latency from 900ms to 240ms beats improved performance. Anything you improved, state the before and the after, and where a number is genuinely unknown say so rather than inventing one.

tips.title: One bullet, one line, 15 to 30 words
tips.body: A bullet that wraps to three lines is a paragraph nobody reads. Aim for 15 to 30 words and keep it scannable top to bottom.

tips.title: Finish with a line about you
tips.body: A single Interests line at the end makes you a person rather than a faceless CV, lets the reader picture you as a coworker, and hands the interviewer an easy opener. One line is the whole point.

tips.title: Tailor lightly, not wildly
tips.body: Change your title, your first bullet, and the order of your skills. Change everything and you will drive yourself mad, and the resume stops sounding like you.

tips.title: Titles may be adjusted
tips.body: Software Engineer can honestly become Front-End Software Engineer if that is what you do. It signals relevance without misrepresenting anything. Never invent a role you did not hold.

tips.title: Black on white, one column
tips.body: No colour, no sidebars, no quadrants. Layout the eye expects is the layout the eye scans fastest, and that is the only one worth optimising for.

tips_note: The NEWS panel on the front page renders this list. It is served from rules.json and injected into the page by the server rather than written into the markup, so advice on screen is the researched advice in RULES.md and not a paraphrase typed from memory.

safe_headings.publications_note: Publications is listed because SPEC section 3 defines an optional Publications section and it is a conventional ATS-recognised heading. The sourcing below does not cover it specifically, so treat that one entry as a design decision rather than a cited rule.
safe_headings.interests_note: Interests is listed because the sheets resume template renders a one-line Interests field, and its source gives three reasons for it: it forces the screener to see a person rather than a faceless CV, it lets them picture you as a coworker, and it is a ready-made interview icebreaker. The heading itself is not independently sourced.

banned_phrases_note: The 23 banned phrases above came from Stage 0 research (RULES.md), NOT from the sheetsresume.com guide. The guide mentions avoiding 'fluff' and 'weak words' generally but does not publish a specific list.

bullet_rules.structure: action_verb + what + how_tool + measurable_result (XYZ: accomplished X, measured by Y, by doing Z)
bullet_rules.quantification: report real scale/metrics only (users, latency, cost, time, revenue, team size); if no number, state scope of work. NEVER invent numbers.

ai_tells.action: warn only — tell the user these words sound AI-generated and suggest plainer alternatives

company_overview_bullet.description: Lead with a bullet about your employer's scale (Fortune 500, revenue, users, employees) to anchor the screener on big numbers. Text comes ONLY from user input — never from model knowledge. Interview mode asks for it.

strongest_bullet_first.definition: Warn only if some bullet in the entry has a metric and the first bullet does not. Do not warn if no bullet has a metric, or if the first bullet already does.
strongest_bullet_first.action: warning — the first bullet is the anchor; the strongest metric should lead

ai_scope.description: Bullet writing (polish + structure) is allowed only for Experience, Projects, and Achievements/Extracurriculars. For Education and Contact, the AI may only structure what the user typed — no polishing, no added wording.

tailoring.description: Light tailoring only. You may change: (a) job title — only with an explicit confirm dialog; (b) the anchor/first bullet; (c) the order of skills. Do NOT rewrite the whole resume per application. Do NOT misrepresent yourself.

gpa.include_if: GPA >= 87.5% of scale (equivalent to 3.5/4.0 or 8.75/10 CGPA)
gpa.india: keep CGPA format, report both CGPA/10 and converted /4.0

contact_rules.no_references_note: Do not include 'References available upon request' or a references section. Provide references separately if explicitly asked.
contact_rules.photo_note: No photo on resume by default (US/UK/CA/AU/NZ/IE anti-discrimination laws). Only include if a country explicitly requires it.
contact_rules.portfolio_note: Portfolio link goes in contact links at the top, alongside name/email/phone/location. Hyperlink descriptive text ('Portfolio', 'GitHub').
contact_rules.linkedin_note: Omit LinkedIn by default. It opens the application to visual bias/discrimination. Exception: executive-level with strong, current profile.

photo.note: not expected for private-sector; only if explicitly asked

personal_fields.legacy_note: Biodata-style fields are common in older Indian formats and some legacy guides; they are not required for ATS/global resumes.

india_specific.portals_parsing_note: Reverse-chronological, parser-safe formats get reportedly ~3x more callbacks (vendor data, treat cautiously); 'verified' only for the direction, not the multiplier.
india_specific.tracker_source_field_note: Cache Indian sources in tracker: Naukri, Instahyre, Foundit, LinkedIn, referral, portal, career fair.

ai_detection_honesty.summary: Detectors unreliable; ~80% of hiring managers claim they can spot AI resumes; ~19.6% reject outright; 62% reject un-personalized AI resumes. Recruiters care about authenticity, not AI use per se. Defense = user's own facts, numbers, vocabulary, and human review. No detector-evasion features.

market_snapshot.stale_warning: Machine-checkable: stale_after is the collected date plus stale_after_days, and data is stale ON that date. Compare today >= stale_after; if so this block must be re-researched before it is shown to the user.
global_trends: top listed AI skills: LangChain, RAG, PyTorch
